cadence: monthly, generated automatically from live platform signals
philosophy: Adoption is a platform metric, not a tenant grade. A criterion that many teams fail is a platform defect before it is a team problem.

criteria.question: Do all model calls go through the AI gateway?
criteria.source: litellm spend logs reconciled against the Azure OpenAI invoice
criteria.passing: 100% of spend attributable to a virtual key
criteria.why: This is the load-bearing criterion. Every other guarantee the platform makes — budgets, entitlement, failover, caching, cost attribution, central audit — is enforced at the gateway. A team that bypasses it is outside all of them at once.

criteria.question: Is there a golden set gating CI?
criteria.passing: >= 15 cases including safety cases, and the gate blocks the merge
criteria.why: For a non-deterministic system this is the only release control that means anything. Without it, the first person to notice a quality regression is a customer.

criteria.question: Are the platform guardrails enabled on the deployed revision?
criteria.passing: input and output pipelines both enabled, no per-tenant override
criteria.why: Guardrails are shared so that a tenant team does not have to reimplement PII redaction to ship. Disabling them silently moves risk from the platform to the company.

criteria.question: Are traces, metrics and audit records arriving?
criteria.source: Log Analytics ingestion + Prometheus target health
criteria.passing: all three present for the deployed revision
criteria.why: An agent you cannot trace is an agent you cannot debug, cost, or defend in a complaint.

criteria.question: Is every resource under Terraform?
criteria.why: Drift means something changed outside the pipeline. That is either an incident or a bug, and both are worth closing.

criteria.question: Is spend capped, attributed and cached?
criteria.passing: daily budget set within 2x of actual, cost centre tagged, cache hit rate >= 15%
criteria.why: A budget set at ten times actual is not a budget. Cache hit rate is the cheapest quality-neutral cost lever there is.

criteria.question: Is the deployed image clean and signed?
criteria.source: Trivy on the deployed digest, cosign verification, gitleaks history
criteria.passing: no CRITICAL/HIGH with a fix available, signature verifies, no secrets in history
criteria.why: An unsigned image in production means the supply chain has an unowned gap.

criteria.question: Is every side-effecting tool gated on a human?
criteria.passing: 100% of tools with side_effect=true also have requires_approval=true
criteria.why: EU AI Act Art. 14, expressed as a property of the code rather than a policy document.

bands.meaning: Fully on the golden path; ships without platform involvement.
On the platform with known gaps; one or two backlog items.
Real risk somewhere; platform team pairs with the tenant.
Not eligible for production traffic until it improves.

open_items: Cache hit rate is 19% against a 25% target — the semantic threshold at 0.93 is rejecting near-duplicate order-status phrasings. Tuning to 0.90 is on the platform backlog with a regression test attached.
